name: WisdomTree, Inc.

profile.description: WisdomTree is a global financial innovator offering exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and exchange-traded products (ETPs) across equity, fixed income, commodity, currency and digital-asset strategies. Founder and CEO Jonathan Steinberg has led the firm since 1988. In Q3 2026, reported October 30, ending AUM reached a record $171.0B, net inflows were $4.6B, operating revenue was $179.4M (about +43% YoY) and diluted EPS was $0.32. Market cap approximately $3.1B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): over five years WisdomTree has moved beyond U.S. smart-beta ETFs into European ETPs, model portfolios, the WisdomTree Prime digital platform and, in 2026, a private-markets vehicle (WisdomTree Private Markets & Innovation Fund I) [1][2]. Revenue grew from $249.9M in 2020 to $493.8M in 2025 [4]. AI Deployment (0/2): its AI exposure is investment products such as the AI & Innovation fund (WTAI), not AI deployed in its own operations with quantified savings [2]. Market Share (1/2): record AUM of $171.0B and year-to-date inflows above $13.6B (a 13% annualized organic growth rate) show share momentum, but the firm remains far smaller than the largest ETF sponsors [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): tokenization and private-markets products are active, but there are no named launches with revenue targets. R&D Intensity (0/1): no meaningful R&D line is reported ($0 in FY2025) [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): WisdomTree presents itself as a 'global financial innovator' building next-generation investment access through ETFs and tokenization [1]. That clearly states what it does but does not set it apart from other asset managers. Community Impact (0/2): no distinctive foundation, charitable program or dollar-quantified community investment was found. Employee Retention (0/2): no turnover or tenure data was found, and the few Glassdoor reviews are mixed, including a 3.0 rating criticizing sales culture and pay [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP insider statistics show net disposals over the last four quarters, including 145,000 shares disposed in Q2 2026 and 30,000 in Q3 2026 with no open-market purchases [5]. CEO Steinberg does hold a substantial 6.93% stake worth about $104M [2].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically using growth-sleeve weights (weighted sum 8.56 of 10, rounded to 9). Growth and returns are strong: revenue growth of 42.8% YoY (Q3 2026 revenue of $179.4M vs $125.6M a year earlier), a 14.6% 5-year revenue CAGR ($249.9M in 2020 to $493.8M in 2025, 2x weight) and ROE of 27.0% (2x weight) all score 1.00 [1][4][6]. Forward P/E of 15.4 scores 1.00, Forward PEG of 1.54 (as reported by Yahoo Finance, 2x weight) scores 0.73, and profit margin of 16.6% scores 0.83 [6]. The main drag is leverage: D/E of 238% (about $1.06B total debt against $341M cash) scores only 0.27 [6]. Liquidity is about $53M per day, well above the floor.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): WisdomTree's revenue comes from asset-based fees on regulated, exchange-listed products, protected by SEC and European registration, exchange listings and brokerage-platform distribution. Its rules-based index strategies do not depend on human stock-picking that AI could replace [1]. The risk is fee compression and commoditization if AI-driven portfolio construction makes factor and thematic strategies easier to replicate; WisdomTree's own research notes that in thematic investing 'disruption isn't the exception, it's the rule' [2]. No analyst coverage flagging AI as a direct threat to WisdomTree was found. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI-themed ETFs such as WTAI earn fees on AI-themed assets, but the firm does not sell AI products or services and discloses no AI revenue [2].

infinite_game.summary: WisdomTree is well run and has adapted well, moving from smart-beta ETFs into European ETPs, tokenized funds and private markets under a founder-CEO with 37 years at the helm. Through Sinek's lens it is still playing mostly to grow AUM rather than to advance a cause people would sacrifice for. Its purpose language is generic for the industry, its strategic moves are opportunity-driven, and the 2024 SEC fine for ESG funds that held fossil-fuel and tobacco stocks contrary to their prospectuses shows a gap between stated values and execution.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): WisdomTree's 'financial innovator' purpose is real, but it is interchangeable with peers and is not framed as a future state the firm serves beyond its own growth [1]. Strategic decisions such as digital-asset products, tokenization and private markets track market opportunities more than a defining cause. The 2024 SEC finding that its ESG funds held fossil-fuel and tobacco issuers contrary to prospectus statements shows stated purposes have not always shaped behavior [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): the organization is stable, with founder-CEO Jonathan Steinberg in place since 1988 (37 years) and a recent appointment of a Global Head of HR, Beena Joseph, framed around 'culture-powered growth' [2]. The firm promotes a 'work smart' model and investment in training. Employee evidence is thin and mixed, however, with Glassdoor reviews citing a weak sales culture and pay alongside praise for culture and benefits [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): no management commentary was found that frames larger ETF sponsors as rivals whose strengths push WisdomTree to improve. The positioning emphasizes differentiation and share gains through innovation and inflows [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): WisdomTree has stretched well beyond its original U.S. dividend-weighted ETF franchise into European ETPs, digital-asset products, the WisdomTree Prime digital platform and private markets [1][2]. The core ETF fee model is intact, however, so these are meaningful adjacencies rather than a reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): leadership has spent for years on tokenization and the Prime digital platform, which have not yet produced material revenue, and has accepted elevated leverage (D/E 238%) while broadening its product set [1][6]. These are long-dated bets, but they are calculated growth investments rather than a pattern of sacrificing profit for a cause.

investment_thesis: WisdomTree is compounding at an unusual rate for an asset manager. Q3 2026 ending AUM hit a record $171.0B (+5% quarter over quarter, roughly +25% YoY from $137.2B), net inflows were $4.6B, and year-to-date inflows above $13.6B represent a 13% annualized organic growth rate [1]. Operating revenue of $179.4M was up about 43% YoY, the adjusted operating margin reached 43.1% on an 83% gross margin, and adjusted EPS of $0.23 beat the $0.21 consensus [1]. At 15.4x forward earnings with 27% ROE, the stock is inexpensive relative to its growth, and the Inspire Impact Score of 52 (ALIGNED, no negative attributions) makes it accessible to faith-based investors [6].
thesis_continued: The bear case is leverage and sensitivity to markets. D/E of 238%, with about $1.06B of debt against $341M of cash, magnifies downside if a market drawdown cuts AUM-based fees [6]. Revenue yield slipped 1 basis point to 0.42% in Q3 on lower European ETP transaction and performance fees, and the 2025-2026 revenue jump is tied to market-sensitive AUM that may not keep compounding at this pace [1]. The October 2024 $4M SEC penalty for ESG ETFs that held fossil-fuel and tobacco stocks contrary to their prospectuses is a reminder of compliance risk [3]. Insiders have been net sellers over the last four quarters [5], and the tokenization platforms have yet to show material revenue.
key_catalysts: Continued record inflows: $13.6B year to date in 2026 (13% annualized organic growth) on a $171.0B AUM base sets up further operating leverage at a 43% adjusted operating margin [1]
Monetization of the WisdomTree Prime digital platform and newer private-markets vehicles, which would diversify revenue beyond traditional ETP fees [1][2]
Deleveraging from strong free cash flow, which would ease the 238% D/E ratio and could support a re-rating from 15.4x forward earnings [6]
key_risks: Market and commodity drawdown risk: with about $1.06B of debt, a sharp fall in AUM-linked fees (especially in commodity and European ETPs) would compress margins and strain the balance sheet [1][6]
Revenue yield erosion: yield fell 1 basis point to 0.42% in Q3 2026 on lower European transaction and performance fees, and industry-wide ETF fee compression could continue [1]
Regulatory and reputational risk after the 2024 SEC $4M settlement over ESG fund screening failures, especially as WisdomTree expands into less-tested tokenized and private-market products [3]
